title: add-benchmark-lab-profiling-baselines-and-reporting-pipeline-v116
author: Priya Narayanan
description:
Motivation: bring profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and an upgraded reporting pipeline into the benchmark-lab to reduce drift between lab results and production traffic patterns. This PR bundles: 1) new baseline definitions for cold-start and steady-state profiling (v116), 2) representative workload runners for mixed-latency and throughput scenarios, 3) an improved reporting pipeline that emits summarized metrics to BigQuery and the internal perf-dashboard, and 4) minor telemetry instrumentation to reduce sampling variance.

What I changed (high level):
- benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v116: adds YAML workload definitions for cold-start, warm-run, and burst scenarios with explicit sequence-length distributions and input mix.
- benchmark-lab/runners/representative_runners.py: new runner that composes request mixes (chat/gen/embeddings) and drives KV-cache/cold-start variants.
- telemetry/reporting/pipeline_v2/config.yaml: reporting job configuration for daily aggregation and Quality-of-Service buckets.
- telemetry/reporting/bigquery_job.py: transforms and uploads summarized token/latency/cost histograms to BigQuery, including schema migration helper.
- docs/benchmark-lab/README.md: usage, expected signal, and how to add new baselines.

Checklist:
- [x] Baseline definitions reviewed with research (Maya) and runtime (Ethan)
- [x] End-to-end test in benchmark-lab CI (smoke)
- [x] Validate BigQuery upload with staging dataset
- [x] Tracing spans added for runner start/end and reporting job

Backward compatibility and rollout: all new baseline files are additive and guarded behind a feature flag benchmark_lab_v116. The new reporting pipeline runs in parallel to the existing pipeline until a promotion window (2 days) completes and no schema regressions observed. No runtime code paths used by production inference were modified, only benchmark tooling, so this is non-breaking.

Notes: the BigQuery schema change is additive (new columns for qos_bucket) and the migration helper is included in the PR. We'll coordinate data retention and dashboard queries with Growth Analytics. Linear references: ENG-4021 (profiling baselines v116), ENG-4100 (reporting pipeline upgrade).
